subject.title: [Feature]: Add JSON-RPC bindings for language-agnostic plugins

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class JSON-RPC child-process plugin ABI as a public Plugin SDK and manifest contract, and at what initial scope?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it adds a public SDK/protocol surface plus a child-process trust boundary that affects plugin compatibility, host permissions, lifecycle, and long-term support.

options.title: Accept protocol v1 after owner review
options.body: Review and land the linked PR if maintainers are ready to support the manifest field, protocol shapes, host-permission model, and process lifecycle contract.

options.title: Narrow or gate the ABI
options.body: Keep the issue open but reduce the initial supported registrations or keep the surface experimental until the compatibility and security boundary are smaller.

options.title: Defer the public ABI
options.body: Leave the feature as a design record if maintainers are not ready to own a language-neutral child-process plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Accept protocol v1 after owner review
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR if maintainers are ready to support the manifest field, protocol shapes, host-permission model, and process lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: RomneyDa owns the companion implementation candidate and can best answer the intended protocol-v1 scope before broader owner review.
